text:
mei: Running a small bring-up for atlas-9b int3 vs int5 focused on short-form customer support answers. Goal: decide if int5 is worth default for support route.
oscar: What's the sample size?
mei: 3k support queries, split evenly. Metrics: answer_accuracy (binary), response_length, and time-to-first-token.
jamie: Cost delta?
mei: int3 ~ $10/1M, int5 ~ $28/1M -> delta $18/1M. Median tokens per response ~ 7k. Extra cost per response ~ $0.000126. Blended across production volume this is small.
vera: Quality diff: int5 +1.8% accuracy, F1 on entity extraction up +4.2%. Latency p95 +60ms.
ci-bot: artifact uploaded -> s3://redwood-evals/atlas/1744445555/artifact.tar.gz sha256:abc987
mei: Product mapping: support accuracy seems to reduce average handle time by ~3% in past pilots -> cost savings for ops. If we multiply by agent cost, potential savings per MAU ~ $0.02 mo.
oscar: So net ROI likely positive if we apply to the support route since token cost is tiny.
jamie: Ops rec: enable atlas-9b-int5 for support route only, with fallback to int3 on latency spike or OOM. Also propose a quick canary (7d) and sample for edge cases (attachments, logs).
vera: Add a QA test for entity extraction regressions as we onboard.
mei: I'll prepare the rollout PR and short sales blurb. Thanks.
